helpers.name: slug_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A ROW, built by `site_path/2`: a `:lang` in the base is filled with the language of
# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not
# publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than a link to a 404.
case site_path(to_string(base) <> "/:slug", %{"lang" => trimmed(language), "slug" => to_string(slug)}) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    case {trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path
      {key, code} -> path <> "?" <> URI.encode_query(%{key => code})
    end
end

helpers.name: narrow
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

query = narrow_language(query, asked.language)

query =
  case asked.featured_only do
    true -> Ash.Query.filter(query, featured == true)
    false -> query
  end

# THE ROW THE HEADING NAMES IS THE ROW THE LIST IS OF. A slug is unique per SITE and not per
# language, so `filter_row/1` resolves it in the page's language — and narrowed by the slug alone
# this listed the Persian posts filed under an English category beneath the page's fallback
# heading, having just decided that category does not exist in Persian. Empty and `all` narrow
# nothing, the same two answers `only_language/2` gives.
query =
  case {asked.collection, asked.language} do
    {"", _the_whole_archive} ->
      query

    {wanted, code} when code not in ["", "all"] ->
      Ash.Query.filter(
        query,
        exists(collections, slug == ^wanted and status == :active and language == ^code)
      )

    {wanted, _every_language} ->
      Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(collections, slug == ^wanted and status == :active))
  end

query =
  case {asked.tag, asked.language} do
    {"", _the_whole_archive} ->
      query

    {wanted, code} when code not in ["", "all"] ->
      Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(tags, slug == ^wanted and language == ^code))

    {wanted, _every_language} ->
      Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(tags, slug == ^wanted))
  end

case asked.exclude_slug do
  "" -> query
  wanted -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug != ^wanted)
end

helpers.code:
# A ROW NAMED BY SLUG IS NARROWED BY THE PAGE'S LANGUAGE, NOT BY THE EDITION RULE. A slug names
# one category or one tag per site whatever language it is written in, so the master-editions
# default `narrow_language/2` applies to a listing would be meaningless here — while no narrowing
# at all headed /fa/blog/category/<english slug> with the English category's name, over the nothing
# that category holds in Persian.
require Ash.Query

case trimmed(wanted) do
  "" -> query
  "all" -> query
  code -> Ash.Query.filter(query, language == ^code)
end

helpers.name: filter_row
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

row =
  cond do
    not asked.show_filter_title ->
      nil

    asked.collection != "" ->
      MishkaBlog.Collection
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(asked.visitor))
      |> Ash.Query.filter(slug == ^asked.collection)
      |> only_language(asked.language)
      |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :name, :description])
      |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
      |> first_row()

    asked.tag != "" ->
      MishkaBlog.Tag
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(asked.visitor))
      |> Ash.Query.filter(slug == ^asked.tag)
      |> only_language(asked.language)
      |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :name, :description])
      |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
      |> first_row()

    true ->
      nil
  end

case row do
  nil -> nil
  found -> %{name: found.name, description: found.description}
end

helpers.name: asked
helpers.code:
# EVERYTHING THE READ DEPENDS ON, AS ONE TERM — AND EVERYTHING A ROW IS DRAWN FROM, which is the
# same term for a reason. It is the argument the task is handed — a plain map rather than the
# socket, so nothing of LiveView's is copied into another process — and it is also what says
# whether anything has to be read at all: `update_many/1` runs on every render of the page holding
# this block, and a block that re-read on each of them would restart its own load whenever
# something else on the page moved.
#
# A STREAMED ROW IS RENDERED ONCE AND NEVER AGAIN. LiveView prunes `stream.inserts` after each
# render, so `@streams.posts` is empty on every render that is not a fresh load and the rows
# already on the page are never rebuilt. An attribute the ROWS read — the variant they are laid out
# in, the words inside them, the bases their links are built from — therefore cannot reach them by
# re-rendering, so it goes in here instead: a change to one re-reads and re-streams. Words OUTSIDE
# the rows (`heading`, `empty_text`, the pager's labels) are free, because those are drawn afresh
# every render.
#
# `params` is the one that stays out, deliberately. The rows take a single key from it — the one
# naming the open post — and each row overwrites that key with its own slug, so a reader opening a
# post BESIDE this list changes `params` without changing a single href. In it, every such click
# would send the whole list back to the database and back to its skeleton.
%{
  visitor: assigns[:current_user],
  language: trimmed(assigns[:language]),
  featured_only: assigns[:featured_only] == true,
  collection: trimmed(assigns[:collection]),
  tag: trimmed(assigns[:tag]),
  exclude_slug: trimmed(assigns[:exclude_slug]),
  show_filter_title: assigns[:show_filter_title] == true,
  sort: trimmed(assigns[:sort]),
  per_page: positive(assigns[:per_page], 5),
  page: asked_page(assigns),
  variant: trimmed(assigns[:variant]),
  show_excerpt: assigns[:show_excerpt] == true,
  show_date: assigns[:show_date] == true,
  read_text: trimmed(assigns[:read_text]),
  featured_text: trimmed(assigns[:featured_text]),
  base: trimmed(assigns[:base]),
  post_base: trimmed(assigns[:post_base]),
  lang_param: trimmed(assigns[:lang_param]),
  post_param: trimmed(assigns[:post_param])
}

helpers.name: fetch
helpers.code:
# RUN IN THE TASK, so nothing here may touch the socket. A page nobody has is clamped to the last
# one there is, and the answer carries the term it was read for — `arrived/2` stores that rather
# than what was asked, so a clamp settles instead of asking again on the next render.
with {:ok, %{rows: posts, total: total}} <- posts_page(asked, asked.page, asked.per_page) do
  pages = max(ceil(total / asked.per_page), 1)

  case asked.page > pages do
    false ->
      {:ok,
       %{
         asked: asked,
         page: asked.page,
         posts: posts,
         total: total,
         pages: pages,
         filter_row: filter_row(asked)
       }}

    true ->
      with {:ok, %{rows: clamped}} <- posts_page(asked, pages, asked.per_page) do
        {:ok,
         %{
           asked: %{asked | page: pages},
           page: pages,
           posts: clamped,
           total: total,
           pages: pages,
           filter_row: filter_row(asked)
         }}
      end
  end
end

helpers.name: cold?
helpers.code:
# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every
# block on it and then throws the rows away, because the mount that follows reads them again.
socket.private[:runtime_cold] == true

helpers.name: load
helpers.code:
asked = asked(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case cold?(socket) or is_nil(before) do
      true ->
        arrived(socket, fetch(asked))

      false ->
        socket
        |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loading: true, failed: false)
        |> MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(:posts, fn -> fetch(asked) end)
    end
end

helpers.name: missing!

# NOTHING ANSWERS AT AN ADDRESS THAT NAMED SOMETHING. On the very first render there is no socket
# to send anything over, so this raises and Phoenix draws the 404 page with a 404 status, exactly as
# it does for a controller.
#
# ONCE CONNECTED IT ASKS THE PAGE TO ASK AGAIN. Raising into a live render crashes the view, and on
# a `patch` the client remounts straight back into the same missing subject and crashes again. A
# LiveComponent has no `handle_params/3` of its own, so it tells the LiveView the way the guides say
# to — `send/2` — and `MishkaCmsWeb.Live.RuntimeLive` answers with a full load of the same address,
# which arrives here as the first-render case above.
if Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) do
  # THE PAGE KNOWS ITS OWN ADDRESS AND THIS DOES NOT: a LiveComponent's assigns are its own, not
  # the LiveView's, so the message carries nothing and the answer is given where the path lives.
  send(self(), :mishka_runtime_not_found)

else
  raise MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError,

end

helpers.name: load_post
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

assigns = socket.assigns
slug = asked_slug(assigns)

post =
  case slug in [nil, ""] do
    true ->
      nil

    false ->
      MishkaBlog.BlogPost
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(assigns[:current_user]))
      |> Ash.Query.filter(slug == ^to_string(slug))
      |> only_language(assigns[:language])
      |> Ash.Query.select([
        :id,
        :title,
        :subtitle,
        :slug,
        :excerpt,
        :content,
        :published_at,
        :updated_at,
        :featured_image_url,
        :featured,
        :language,
        :language_group_id,
        :reading_time_minutes
      ])
      |> Ash.Query.load([:rendered_content])
      |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
      |> first_row()
  end

# A SLUG THE URL NAMED AND NOTHING ANSWERS IS A MISSING PAGE, not a page with a notice on it.
# The address was a post; there is no post; 404 is the honest answer and the one a crawler needs —
# see `MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError`, which every other "not here" in this CMS
# raises. LiveView converts it exactly as a controller does: on the HTTP render Phoenix's error view
# draws the 404 page, and on a connected render the client reloads into that same answer.
#
# ONLY WHEN THE URL NAMED IT. A slug an author typed into the `slug` attribute of an embedded card
# is their content mistake, and taking the whole page down for it would be a worse answer than the
# notice — so that case still draws `missing_text`.
if post == nil and slug not in [nil, ""] and from_url?(assigns) do
  missing!(socket)
end

# NOTHING IS READ FOR A PART THE PAGE TURNED OFF. `update/2` runs again on every re-render of the
# page holding this component, so a page drawing the body alone paid for four reads it never showed,
# every single time.
socket
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:slug, slug)
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:post, post)
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:tags, (assigns[:show_tags] && tags_of(post, assigns[:current_user])) || [])
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:categories, (assigns[:show_categories] && categories_of(post, assigns[:current_user])) || [])
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:authors, (assigns[:show_authors] && authors_of(post, assigns[:current_user])) || [])
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(
  :translations,
  (assigns[:show_translations] && translations(post, assigns[:current_user])) || []
)

# THE ROWS `blog-term-row` DRAWS, prepared here because only this block knows which base each
# kind of row is addressed under. A base nobody gave means a word rather than a link, which is what
# a block that does not own the router can honestly offer. Neither kind ever patches: a category
# and a tag lead to a page of their own or to nothing.
case trimmed(base) do
  "" ->
    Enum.map(rows, &%{name: &1.name, href: nil, patch: nil, hreflang: nil})

  address ->
    Enum.map(
      rows,
      &%{

helpers.name: translation_links
helpers.args: rows, post_base, base, params, post_param, lang_param
helpers.code:
# AN EDITION LEADS TO ITS OWN LANGUAGE'S ADDRESS where posts have pages of their own, and opens
# beside this one where they do not — and the second is a PATCH, which is what keeps the page
# holding this block mounted while the article under it changes. `navigate` would remount it, and
# the two are the same href, so nothing but the reload says which one was drawn.
#
# A TRANSLATIONS ROW SAYS WHAT EXISTS, so an edition this site has no URL for stays in it as a word
# — `slug_href/4` makes none for a language the site does not publish. That is the truth about it:
# the translation was written, this site does not serve it. Offering it as a link would send the
# reader to a 404 instead.
Enum.map(rows, fn row ->
  {address, beside} =
    case {trimmed(post_base), trimmed(base)} do
      {"", ""} -> {nil, nil}
      {"", _beside_this_one} -> {nil, href(base, params, post_param, row.slug)}
      {own_page, _either} -> {slug_href(own_page, row.slug, lang_param, row.language), nil}
    end

  %{
    name: row.language,
    href: address,
    patch: beside,
    hreflang: row.language
  }
end)

require Ash.Query

# THE REPLIES ARE READ AS THE COMMENTS ABOVE THEM ARE, through the public action and as the
# visitor. `replies` itself reads through the resource's primary action, which is the moderators'.
replies =
  MishkaBlog.Comment
  |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
  |> Ash.Query.load(:rendered_content)

# ONE CAPPED PAGE AT A TIME. `:approved_by_post` hands back at most 100 rows and Ash shrinks a
# bigger ask to that cap rather than refusing it, so asking for the whole conversation at once made
# every comment past the hundredth unreachable while "load more" stayed on the page for ever.
Enum.reduce_while(Stream.iterate(0, &(&1 + 100)), {:ok, {[], 0}}, fn offset, {:ok, {gathered, counted}} ->
  ask = min(wanted - offset, 100)

  MishkaBlog.Comment
  |> Ash.Query.for_read(:approved_by_post, %{post_id: post_id}, read_as(visitor))
  |> Ash.Query.filter(is_nil(parent_comment_id))
  |> Ash.Query.sort(is_pinned: :desc, inserted_at: :asc)
  |> Ash.Query.load([:rendered_content, replies: replies])
  |> Ash.read(
    tenant: site_id(),
    page: [limit: ask, offset: offset, count: offset == 0]
  )
  |> paged()
  |> case do
    {:error, reason} ->
      {:halt, {:error, reason}}

    {:ok, %{rows: page, total: total}} ->
      rows = gathered ++ page

      whole =
        case offset do
          0 -> total
          _a_later_page -> counted
        end

      case length(rows) < wanted and length(page) == ask do
        true -> {:cont, {:ok, {rows, whole}}}
        false -> {:halt, {:ok, {rows, whole}}}
      end
  end
end)

# THE ADDRESS OF A ROW, built by `site_path/2`: a `:lang` in the base is filled with the language of
# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not
# publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than a link to a 404.
case site_path(to_string(base) <> "/:slug", %{"lang" => trimmed(language), "slug" => to_string(slug)}) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    case {trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path
      {key, code} -> path <> "?" <> URI.encode_query(%{key => code})

end

# A PAGE NOBODY HAS IS CLAMPED TO THE LAST ONE THERE IS, and the answer carries the term it was read
# for, as the list's does, so a clamp settles instead of asking again on the next render.
case listed.wanted and listed.slug != "" do
  false ->
    {:ok, %{listed: listed, posts: [], page: 1, pages: 1}}

  true ->
    with {:ok, %{rows: posts, total: total}} <- posts_page(listed, listed.page) do
      pages = max(ceil(total / listed.per_page), 1)

      case listed.page > pages do
        false ->
          {:ok, %{listed: listed, posts: posts, page: listed.page, pages: pages}}

        true ->
          with {:ok, %{rows: clamped}} <- posts_page(listed, pages) do
            {:ok, %{listed: %{listed | page: pages}, posts: clamped, page: pages, pages: pages}}
          end
      end
    end
end

# A PAGE NOBODY HAS IS CLAMPED TO THE LAST ONE THERE IS, and the answer carries the term it was read
# for, as the list's does, so a clamp settles instead of asking again on the next render.
case listed.wanted and listed.slug != "" do
  false ->
    {:ok, %{listed: listed, posts: [], page: 1, pages: 1}}

  true ->
    with {:ok, %{rows: posts, total: total}} <- posts_page(listed, listed.page) do
      pages = max(ceil(total / listed.per_page), 1)

      case listed.page > pages do
        false ->

        true ->
          with {:ok, %{rows: clamped}} <- posts_page(listed, pages) do
            {:ok, %{listed: %{listed | page: pages}, posts: clamped, page: pages, pages: pages}}
          end
      end
    end
end

components.template: {@label} <.link :for={term <- @terms} :if={term[:href] || term[:patch]} navigate={term[:href]} patch={term[:patch]} hreflang={term[:hreflang]} data-role={@item_role} class={[ "rounded-full border border-[#ecebe6] px-3 py-1 font-semibold text-[#5b57d6] hover:bg-[#f2f1fc]", @uppercase && "uppercase" ]} > {term.name} {term.name}

opts.doc: The words in front of the row. Left empty, none are drawn.

What to draw, as the block above prepared it: a list of maps carrying name, href, patch and hreflang. A term with an href leads away, one with a patch opens beside this page, and one with neither is drawn as a word.
The data-role the row itself carries, so the block around it names the row as well as its words — blog-detail-tags, say.
The data-role each word carries, so the block around it names its own rows — blog-detail-tag, say.
Draw each word in capitals, which is what a row of language codes wants.
Leave a wider gap above the row, which is what the first row under an article wants.

components.name: blog-pager
components.description: A function component: the pager under a list — first, previous, where the reader is, next, last. Written as links when the list has a URL of its own and as buttons aimed at the block above it when it has not.
components.template: 1} {@rest} data-role={@role} aria-label="Pages" class="mt-8 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-2" > <.link :if={trimmed(@base) != ""} patch={page_href(@base, @params, @page_param, 1)} data-role="blog-list-first" class={[ "rounded-full border border-[#ecebe6] bg-white px-3 py-1 text-xs font-semibold", @page <= 1 && "pointer-events-none opacity-40" ]} > {@first_text} <.link :if={trimmed(@base) != ""} patch={page_href(@base, @params, @page_param, @page - 1)} data-role="blog-list-prev" class={[ "rounded-full border border-[#ecebe6] bg-white px-3 py-1 text-xs font-semibold", @page <= 1 && "pointer-events-none opacity-40" ]} > {@previous_text} {@page} / {@pages} <.link :if={trimmed(@base) != ""} patch={page_href(@base, @params, @page_param, @page + 1)} data-role="blog-list-next" class={[ "rounded-full border border-[#ecebe6] bg-white px-3 py-1 text-xs font-semibold", @page >= @pages && "pointer-events-none opacity-40" ]} > {@next_text} <.link :if={trimmed(@base) != ""} patch={page_href(@base, @params, @page_param, @pages)} data-role="blog-list-last" class={[ "rounded-full border border-[#ecebe6] bg-white px-3 py-1 text-xs font-semibold", @page >= @pages && "pointer-events-none opacity-40" ]} > {@last_text}

opts.doc: The page being read.
How many there are. Under two, nothing is drawn.
The path the pager writes its links to. Left empty it draws buttons and sends the click to the block above instead.
The page's own query string, handed straight through, so a link this component writes keeps every key the page already had.
The query key the page number is written under.
The data-role the pager carries, so the block around it names its own — blog-list-pager, say.
Who a button sends its click to — @myself, from the block that drew this.
The jump to the first page.
The step back.
The step forward.
The jump to the last page.

components.description: A function component: one blogger or one team — their picture, their name, their handle and a line about them — as a card or as a small chip. Drawn by blog-author-profile, blog-team-profile and blog-people, which is why it is a component and not markup inside any of them.

<.link :if={@navigate} navigate={@navigate} data-role="blog-profile-name" dir="auto" class="block text-sm font-semibold leading-snug hover:underline" > {@name} {@name} @{@handle}

helpers.name: plain
helpers.code:
# PLAIN TEXT, because a line on a card is not the place for a bio's links and emphasis: what was
# stored is drawn without its tags, its whitespace folded.
case value do
  text when is_binary(text) ->
    text
    |> HtmlSanitizeEx.strip_tags()
    |> String.replace(~r/\s+/u, " ")
    |> String.trim()

  _nothing -> ""
end

stylesheets.name: blog-code-highlight
stylesheets.description: Colours the code blocks in a post: pre.highlight and the token classes Makeup emits, in its Monokai style.
stylesheets.content:
/* Code in a blog post: <pre class="highlight"><code class="language-x"> with one <span> per token.
   The token classes are the ones Makeup emits, coloured in its Monokai style. */
pre.highlight {
  color: #f8f8f2;
  background-color: #272822;
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 16px 20px;
  margin: 0 0 12px;
  overflow-x: auto;
  font-size: 13px;
  line-height: 1.6;
  direction: ltr;
  text-align: left;
  tab-size: 2;
}

pre.highlight code {
  display: block;
  padding: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: inherit;
  font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace;
  font-size: inherit;
  white-space: pre;
}
